conditions: reference_building_id must be one of the three Hazard reference profiles r1 buildings
convective_gust_3s_10m_mph is the 3-second gust at 10 m in open terrain, mph; no terrain or height adjustment in Damage
records are valid from 0 to 255 mph; above 255 withholds; a negative gust is rejected
straight-line damage is zero at or below 96 mph (fixed onset, not location-specific)
straight-line records are a T4 transfer of tornado-derived EF evidence
scenario dollars stay withheld until the consumer qualifies the building value
owner acceptance of the scope and selections is required before any canonical use
reference_building_id must be one of the three Hazard reference profiles r1 buildings
tornado_gust_3s_10m_mph is the 3-second gust at 10 m in open terrain, mph; no terrain or height adjustment in Damage
records are valid from 0 to 255 mph; above 255 withholds; a negative gust is rejected
an EF rating is not an input; Hazard's EF band midpoint gust is accepted as a damage-inferred gust
tornado-specific effects (pressure drop, rotation, debris) are inside the EF observations; no separate add-on
scenario dollars stay withheld until the consumer qualifies the building value
owner acceptance of the scope and selections is required before any canonical use

prerequisites: owner acceptance of scope and curve selections
consumer-qualified replacement cost new for each reference building
Hazard straight-line frequency and tornado hit geometry reviewed (NRI check)

checks_required: record routing by pathway_id and reference_building_id
each pathway reads only its own gust field
a tornado-spawned or hurricane gust is routed to one pathway only (no double count)
all perils on one building in one event together at most 100% of structure value
cap_binding.action_if_fail: withhold the affected DR or downstream metric; do not substitute another record or clamp

required_before_canonical_use: consumer value qualification of each reference budget (shared with flood_real_estate)
reviewer accepts the T4 straight-line transfer and the cost assignment
